Probe Sync Lag: Whole-Edge Misalignment of Spikes

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source
electrophysiology
synchronization
QC
Neuropixels
spikeglx
80 Neuropixels 3B probes on Alyx, 17 of them in the BWM 2023 release, have spike times shifted by whole multiples of 0.5 s because of the probe-to-session sync. Cause, damage report and fix.
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

November 6, 2026

The issue

  • What: on some probes, spike times are shifted by a whole multiple of 0.5 s; behaviour data is correct.
  • Why: the sync is a 1 Hz square wave with an edge every 0.5 s. ibllib version3B pairs probe and nidq edges by index from the start of the file. If SpikeGLX starts the two files k edges apart, spikes shift by k × 0.5 s, and QC still passes.
  • Fix: the lag can be read from the .meta files, and it matches behaviour on 45 of 46 insertions. Correcting it needs no raw data and no re-sorting.

Damage report

Across the 8,689 3B probes on Alyx, 80 probes in 50 sessions are shifted, by −8 to +1 s:

probes
BWM 2023 release 17 of 699
BWM project, outside the release 7 (2 without an insertion)
other projects 56
  • Cause A, 51 probes: one UCLA rig, Aug–Oct 2023, running an old SpikeGLX on newer firmware. All of these are shifted, mostly by +0.5 s. See the UCLA rig report.
  • Cause B, 29 probes: sporadic whole-second shifts, across 8 labs, from 2019 to 2026.

Recommended actions

  1. Data: re-run the probe sync of the 80 shifted probes with the tabulated lag, and warn BWM users meanwhile.
  2. Pipeline: make version3B take the lag from the metadata, and fail QC when it is ambiguous.
  3. Ambiguous probes: check the 25 against behaviour.

Technical details

How the lag is determined

Both files start on the same sync phase, so the lag is a whole number k of half-periods that the edges alone cannot reveal. firstSample is off by up to ~3.6 s before SpikeGLX 20221012, but the error cancels between file start and end:

boundary = (start_lead - end_lead) / 0.5

k = round(boundary) if within 0.25 of an integer and |k| ≤ 20, else 0. This agrees with the edge counts on 781/781 probes, and with the wheel estimate on 45/46.

The UCLA rig (cause A)

  • Software and firmware mismatch. Installing 20230411 on 2023-08-14 flashed firmware BS 169 / BSC 186. The MFD and MM012 experiments kept running 20201103, which ships with BS 137 / BSC 176. They are the only such recordings among 2,450 20201103 probes on Alyx, and all 51 are shifted. Under 20230411, 790 of 790 probes are aligned.
  • Likely mechanism: an inverted sync bit. The lags are odd numbers of edges, yet the first edges carry the same polarity, so the probe reads the sync inverted and the file starts on the wrong edge. The cabling is ruled out, and the release notes say nothing about it.

Behavioural validation

Cross-correlating the population rate with wheel speed (behaviour clock, aperiodic) measures the offset directly. A result counts as confident with SNR ≥ 2 and a bootstrap CI narrower than 0.3 s.

Caveats and reproduction

  • Shifts outside the BWM release come from metadata and are not all checked against behaviour. 3A sessions are out of scope.
  • Scripts are in scripts/, in run order; build_tables.py builds this page. No raw binaries were used.

## The issue

- **What:** on some probes, spike times are shifted by a whole multiple of 0.5 s; behaviour data is correct.
- **Why:** the sync is a 1 Hz square wave with an edge every 0.5 s. `ibllib` `version3B` pairs probe and nidq
  edges by index from the start of the file. If SpikeGLX starts the two files *k* edges apart, spikes shift by
  *k* × 0.5 s, and QC still passes.
- **Fix:** the lag can be read from the `.meta` files, and it matches behaviour on 45 of 46 insertions.
  Correcting it needs no raw data and no re-sorting.

## Damage report

Across the 8,689 3B probes on Alyx, **80 probes in 50 sessions are shifted**, by −8 to +1 s:

| | probes |
|---|---|
| BWM 2023 release | **17** of 699 |
| BWM project, outside the release | 7 (2 without an insertion) |
| other projects | 56 |

- **Cause A, 51 probes:** one UCLA rig, Aug–Oct 2023, running an old SpikeGLX on newer firmware. All of these are
  shifted, mostly by +0.5 s. See the [UCLA rig report](ucla_rig.qmd).
- **Cause B, 29 probes:** sporadic whole-second shifts, across 8 labs, from 2019 to 2026.

```
boundary = (start_lead - end_lead) / 0.5
```

781/781 probes, and with the wheel estimate on 45/46.

### The UCLA rig (cause A)

![churchlandlab_ucla probes in 2023 by SpikeGLX version and base-station firmware. Only `20201103` on firmware `3.2.186` is shifted.](figures/churchland_timeline.png)

- **Software and firmware mismatch.** Installing `20230411` on 2023-08-14 flashed firmware BS 169 / BSC 186. The
  MFD and MM012 experiments kept running `20201103`, which ships with BS 137 / BSC 176. They are the only such
  recordings among 2,450 `20201103` probes on Alyx, and all 51 are shifted. Under `20230411`, 790 of 790 probes
  are aligned.
- **Likely mechanism: an inverted sync bit.** The lags are odd numbers of edges, yet the first edges carry the same
  polarity, so the probe reads the sync inverted and the file starts on the wrong edge. The cabling is ruled out,
  and the release notes say nothing about it.

### Behavioural validation

Cross-correlating the population rate with wheel speed (behaviour clock, aperiodic) measures the offset directly.
A result counts as confident with SNR ≥ 2 and a bootstrap CI narrower than 0.3 s.

![Wheel cross-correlation for the first suspects and controls.](figures/006_wheel_xcorr.png)

### Caveats and reproduction

- Shifts outside the BWM release come from metadata and are not all checked against behaviour. 3A sessions are
  out of scope.
- Scripts are in `scripts/`, in run order; `build_tables.py` builds this page. No raw binaries were used.
